transcript: She thinks of everything. Perrin put the chalk down. That's the other thing. She's watched every lane we've stood since the gate. She knows the elbows. She knows the hen. She knows Price walks her wall from the far end. He looked round at them. She doesn't know Finch calls the pen. Nobody does. We decided it at this table four minutes ago. The graving was full at ten, and half of the full had come to look at a girl who'd dreamed. Kiva felt them as she came out of the side door onto the floor. It was not like Friday. On Friday, the whole town had stood up for Karo, and Kiva had been one of eight people on a floor. Today, it did not stand. It sat, tier after tier, in green and in grey and in the colours of six circuits. And every face in the lower tiers turned as she came out of the door and followed her across the stone to Seven's hurdle. She felt it on the side of her face and the back of her neck like the sun.
